newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi police quell Egyptian pilgrims.
newsitem.headline: Saudi police quell Egyptian pilgrims.

text.p: Saudi police have intervened to calm hundreds of enraged Egyptian Moslem pilgrims and regular travellers who got stranded at Jeddah airport because of seat shortages on Egypt Air, airport sources said on Saturday.
Around 2,000 Egyptians thronged the airport late on Friday to catch their flights to Cairo.

But many, including pilgrims who performd the minor Umra pilgrimage at Mecca and travellers heading to Cairo to spend the Eid al-Fitr holiday marking the end of the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan, could not find seats.

"So many became very angry with Egypt Air ground staff and police had to intervene to end the tension," one source told Reuters by telephone from Saudi. "The crisis of the Umra pilgrims is over. Egypt Air had to send extra flights to pick them up."
He gave no further details and officials were not immediately available for comment.
Diplomats said over 30,000 Egyptian pilgrims performed the Umra this year. The pilgrimage can take place at any time of the year and takes over an hour to complete.
